text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Drinking water at some of Kuwait's old schools is contaminated.
- Some 120 army majors promoted to lieutenant colonels.
- Emir Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah sends National Day congratulations to South Africa.
- Parents complain of rising private school fees.
- Cabinet reviews at weekly meeting status of illegal residents.

- Families of 36 Bangladeshi shepherds killed by mines to be compensated. Tens of thousands of mines were cleared after the 1991 Gulf War to free Kuwait of a seven-month Iraqi occupation but experts say wind-shifted sands make it difficult to ensure that any desert area is fully safe.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to embark on new Arab tour. Mubarak last week visited Kuwait and Saudi Arabia.

- Prime Minister and Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al- Sabah in good health in Italy. Sheikh Saad flew to Britain and later to the United States for medical checks after an emergency colon surgery in Kuwait in early March.
- Kuwait Stock Exchange index shed 10.2 points to 2,328 in a corrective drop.
